discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 021056
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
556 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Light rain showers continue at times through this evening
  (20-30% chances).

- Much better chances for rain (80-100%) arrive late Tuesday
  night into early Wednesday.

- Highs will be well into the 70s on Tuesday with breezy
  conditions but otherwise highs remain around 60 the rest of
  the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 120 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Scattered, light rain showers/drizzle will persist through today as 
broad 295-300K isentropic upglide continues. This isentropic ascent 
is very gentle though and we are still battling some dry air 
concerns so there will be plenty of rain-free areas as well and have 
maintained just broad-brushed 20 PoP's through this evening. Best 
chances appear to be east of I-69 late this afternoon into the 
evening as models indicate another weak shortwave rippling through 
the area. This wave exits overnight and isentropic surfaces orient 
more parallel to increasing southwest flow. Therefore, expect dry 
conditions to return late tonight through most of the day Tue. 
Overcast skies today yield highs only in the low/mid 60s. Tue high 
temp forecast is tricky. Strong SW flow/WAA develops ahead of 
approaching trough but cloud cover is still a question. Some peaks 
of sun are likely, especially in our SE, and this could push highs 
to near record territory (76). Tempered NBM highs downward a bit as 
they are likely biased by the last few weeks of very warm/sunny 
conditions. If full sun materializes then it's possible but expect 
at least some clouds given degree of moisture streaming into 
the region.

Very few changes regarding Tue night's frontal passage. Upper trough 
and low level cyclone will be rapidly lifting and occluding over the 
Upper Midwest late Tue. This combined with surface low track toward 
Lake Superior will support a healthy midlevel dry slot moving into 
the area Wed morning and bringing a quick end to rain. Maintained 
categorical PoP's out of respect for the moisture advection but 
westward displacement of better mid/upper level dynamics and 
southward displacement of any meaningful instability will likely 
leave our area with just some brief, light rain showers late Tue 
night into Wed morning. Rainfall amounts around 0.25" with no 
thunder anticipated. While steady/moderate rain ends Wed afternoon, 
a prolonged period of general cyclonic flow is expected to develop 
Wed night into next week as several upper lows pinwheel through the 
Great Lakes. This supports periodic low chances for light rain, 
particularly downwind of still warm Lake Michigan. The only 
exception looks to be a brief break in between systems on Sat. 
Temps return to more seasonable values to end the week but still
trending slightly above normal with highs around 60 and lows 
around 40.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z TAFS THROUGH 12Z TUESDAY/...
Issued at 556 AM EST Mon Nov 2 2026

Satellite and observing stations indicate MVFR ceilings are
steadily spreading north this morning; quickly closing in on 
KSBN. Observations in central IN and central IL show IFR 
ceilings in place; perhaps not completely out of the realm of 
possibility for our local area for at least a brief time. Weak 
ascent through an increasingly saturated atmosphere still lends
the opportunity for passing light showers or sprinkles today. 
The low level jet strengthens tonight ahead of a mid-latitude 
cyclone moving into the Midwest. LLWS may be a concern through 
most of Tuesday morning before the LLJ eases in the afternoon.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...AGD
AVIATION...Brown

spc.summary: Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes are expected across parts of the southern and central Plains from this afternoon into tonight.
spc.text:
SPC AC 020559

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1159 PM CST Sun Nov 01 2026

   Valid 021200Z - 031200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
   THE SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL PLAINS INTO THE LOWER MISSOURI VALLEY...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts and a few tornadoes
   are expected across parts of the southern and central Plains from
   this afternoon into tonight.

   ...Southern and Central Plains/Ozarks/Lower Missouri Valley...
   An upper-level trough will move across the southern Rockies today
   and into the southern High Plains. Ahead of the system, the exit
   region of a mid-level jet will overspread the southern and central
   Plains this afternoon and evening. At the surface, a cold front will
   advance southeastward across the central High Plains as a
   pre-frontal trough moves into the southern and central Plains. Ahead
   of this feature, moisture advection will take place with surface
   dewpoints gradually increasing into the mid to upper 60s F over much
   of Texas, Oklahoma and the eastern half of Kansas. Across the moist
   sector, RAP forecast soundings suggest that MLCAPE will only peak in
   the 1000 to 1500 J/kg range. As surface temperatures warm and
   low-level convergence becomes maximized near the pre-frontal trough
   in the afternoon, convective development will take place.
   Thunderstorms are expected to gradually increase in coverage from
   the afternoon into the early evening, as several line segments
   organize and move east-northeastward across the moist sector.

   The convective mode is the main question for this event. It seems
   possible that the convection will line out quickly during the
   afternoon, and that discrete cell formation will be minimized. Even
   so, widespread large-scale ascent and strong deep-layer shear will
   likely support severe thunderstorm development with vigorous
   updrafts associated with organized lines and potentially
   semi-discrete supercells. The latest RAP forecast soundings from
   central Oklahoma north-northeastward into eastern Kansas suggest
   that 0-6 km shear will be around 50 knots. Although some directional
   shear is present, the stronger component will be speed increases
   with height in the low-levels. Near the axis of the low-level jet,
   0-3 km storm-relative helicity is forecast to peak in the 250 to 300
   m2/s2 range. This will support a tornado threat with supercells and
   with rotating elements embedded in organized line segments. Severe
   wind gusts will also be possible with the more intense line
   segments, especially with bowing structures. A greater tornado
   threat could materialize across Oklahoma or southeast Kansas, if a
   cluster of discrete cells can persist into the late afternoon or
   early evening. A severe threat will continue throughout the evening
   as a larger-scale line segment moves eastward across the moist
   sector, reaching western Missouri and far eastern Oklahoma around
   midnight. Severe wind gusts and perhaps a QLCS tornado threat will
   be possible with this line.

   ...Texas...
   Southwesterly cyclonic mid-level flow will be in place today across
   much of Texas, as an upper-level trough approaches. Ahead of the
   system, an axis of moderate instability will develop as surface
   temperatures warm. A capping inversion will be in place over much of
   Texas into afternoon. This cap will likely weaken during the mid
   afternoon, allowing for convective initiation over parts of
   west-central and northwest Texas. A convective band, with a mixed
   mode, is expected to form and move eastward into north-central Texas
   by early evening. Ahead of this forecast band by 00Z, surface
   dewpoints are expected to peak in the upper 60s F, with MLCAPE
   reaching the 2000 to 2500 J/kg range. This will be favorable for
   strong updrafts and scattered severe storms. The southeastern edge
   of the mid-level jet will create moderate deep-layer shear along the
   axis of instability. This will support supercell development with
   cells that can remain discrete. Intense line segments are also
   expected with cells that congeal. Severe wind gusts and a couple
   tornadoes will be possible during the late afternoon and early to
   mid evening. The greatest tornado threat should be concentrated in
   north-central Texas where low-level shear is maximized on the
   southern edge of the low-level jet.

   ..Broyles/Weinman.. 11/02/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.summary: Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts, and a brief tornado cannot be ruled out.
spc.text:
SPC AC 020655

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1255 AM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 031200Z - 041200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM FAR EASTERN
   TEXAS AND CENTRAL LOUISIANA INTO SOUTHEAST MISSOURI AND SOUTHWEST
   ILLINOIS...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Scattered storms will occur from the Sabine and Lower Mississippi
   Valleys northward into the Mid Mississippi Valley on Tuesday. A few
   thunderstorms may produce damaging gusts, and a brief tornado cannot
   be ruled out.

   ...Discussion...
   A highly amplified upper trough will move out of the Plains and
   toward the MS Valley on Tuesday, with moderate southerly winds
   aloft. Height falls will occur over MO and AR during the day, and
   into IL and western KY and TN overnight.

   At the surface, low pressure will be located over southern MN,
   nearly stationary, with a front extending south across IA, MO, and
   into the Sabine Valley during the afternoon.

   Southerly low-level winds with 30-40 kt at 850 mb will aid moisture
   transport, with mid 60s F dewpoints as far north as the Missouri
   Bootheel. Rain and thunderstorms will be ongoing along the front
   early, though a diurnal uptick in intensity is expected from the
   Sabine River into southern MO.

   The primary mitigating factor on Tuesday will be widespread clouds,
   rain, and weak lapse rates ahead of the front. Still, at least
   isolated severe gusts, or a brief tornado or two may occur as shear
   profiles overall will favor rotation with storms along the front, or
   possible cells ahead of the front from LA into AR.

   ..Jewell.. 11/02/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 020815

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0215 AM CST Mon Nov 02 2026

   Valid 041200Z - 051200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely on Wednesday.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper low will move from the Upper MS Valley to the Upper Great
   Lakes on Wednesday, with glancing height falls toward the
   Appalachians as a leading speed max aloft ejects northeastward out
   of the OH Valley. A surface low is forecast to move northward out of
   WI and toward Lake Superior, with a weak surface trough/winds shift
   pushing across the Upper OH and TN Valleys during the day.

   While lift/upper support will be minimal over the Southeast, mid to
   upper 60s F dewpoints will support weak instability from AL into GA
   and eastern TN. Given the antecedent surface high over the Mid
   Atlantic, and departure of the upper system, waning large-scale
   support would suggest little severe weather risk. However, scattered
   general thunderstorms are likely near the front as it moves across
   KY/TN/AL/GA.

   ..Jewell.. 11/02/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
